subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add explicit core `first-progress` and `startup-failed` lifecycle phases for sub-agent startup, or solve the silent-startup abort through existing terminal outcome/session semantics?
rationale: Both paths can address the visible hang, but the choice creates or avoids a new core lifecycle event contract across gateway, SDK, session, and subagent consumers.

options.title: Adopt typed startup lifecycle phases
options.body: Add `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` as the canonical contract, then update all current-main consumers and prove a forced startup abort reaches the parent visibly.

options.title: Use existing terminal outcomes
options.body: Keep the public lifecycle phase set unchanged and encode startup abort/progress through existing terminal outcome, session, and wait metadata.

options.title: Defer to sandbox-specific proof first
options.body: Hold the API change until the sandbox-triggered startup stall in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39248 is live-reproduced and narrowed.

recommendation.title: Adopt typed startup lifecycle phases
recommendation.body: Add `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` as the canonical contract, then update all current-main consumers and prove a forced startup abort reaches the parent visibly.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the strongest history across subagent lifecycle and terminal outcome surfaces that would define the permanent contract.
